stories.title: Meituan releases 1.6T-parameter LongCat-2.5 agent model trained without Nvidia GPUs
stories.summary: Meituan released the weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model built for AI agents and trained entirely on Chinese hardware, scoring 88.4 on Terminal-Bench, just behind Claude Opus 5.
stories.more: Meituan has released the weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model designed for AI agents and trained entirely on Chinese hardware. On Terminal-Bench, the model scores 88.4 points, placing it just behind Claude Opus 5. Meituan's sample deployment runs on 194 Huawei Ascend chips, and the company makes no mention of using Nvidia GPUs anywhere in development. Details on training data or cost were not disclosed.

stories.title: Australia's central bank says AI is hitting young workers first
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia finds early signs that AI is displacing young workers fastest in software development and customer service, with job postings for 15- to 24-year-olds falling more sharply than for older workers.
stories.more: Australia's central bank sees early evidence that AI is hitting entry-level workers hardest in fields highly exposed to automation, such as software development and customer service. Since ChatGPT's launch, job postings and employment among 15- to 24-year-olds in those fields have fallen more sharply than among older workers. Report author Mike Major cautions against drawing firm conclusions, noting that business cycle shifts and remote-work trends could also explain the pattern.

stories.title: Carnegie Mellon student's OATs turn household objects into AI pets
stories.summary: A Carnegie Mellon student built OATs, tiny E Ink gadgets that give houseplants, skateboards, and dumbbells expressive virtual personalities to nudge owners toward healthier habits.
stories.more: OATs are small E Ink devices designed to attach to everyday objects like houseplants, skateboards, and dumbbells. Each gadget displays an expressive, Tamagotchi-like personality that reacts to how the object is used, aiming to nudge owners toward better habits. The project comes from a Carnegie Mellon student; further details on availability or release plans were not included in the report.

stories.title: Firm tied to Jensen Huang's ex-partner brokered $12B Nvidia orders for China
stories.summary: A firm owned by Jensen Huang's former partner reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese buyers in 2024-2025, as short sellers argue Nvidia's real China revenue exceeds official figures.
stories.more: The Wall Street Journal reported that Megaspeed, a firm owned by Alice Huang, arranged nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies between 2024 and 2025. Alice Huang is described in the report as Jensen Huang's former lover. Short seller Culper Research estimates Nvidia's actual revenue share from China tops 20 percent, well above the 7 percent Nvidia has officially disclosed. The gap raises questions about how Nvidia chips continue reaching Chinese buyers despite US export restrictions.
